soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 and Open-ended Question 1: asserted PS counterpart
soundness_flags.one_line: The PN finite profile constrains only the control regression while its transformed PS profile would require the transformed control regression 1-u to lie in that spline class; no PS-specific profile class, learner, or closure argument is defined, so applying T does not presently yield the claimed counterpart.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2: lower-bound shell
soundness_flags.one_line: The lower-bound route invokes lem:lf-membership, whose least-favorable construction requires 2\bar d\le1, but this load-bearing rarity-cap condition is neither an assumption nor a hypothesis of thm:lower.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1 marked-Poisson boundary
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The marked-Poisson likelihood-ratio limit is asserted only along finite profile families satisfying the stated rare-mark intensity and common-cell likelihood conditions.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact randomized coverage is unconditional for positive-denominator laws in the finite experiment; the boundary limit is conditional on def:marked-poisson.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a separate PS finite profile with a spline fit for m1 (or enlarge the finite profile so it is explicitly closed under T), then state and verify the swapped likelihood and score construction.
Add 2\bar d\le1 as an explicit class-cap assumption or restate thm:lower on d_n\le1/2; thread that condition through the least-favorable membership proof.
Turn the continuous-transfer handle into a specified continuous-data profile statistic and prove an upper diameter bound on the identical PN shell as thm:lower, creating a genuine matched frontier.

recommended_next_step: Revise the PS construction and the missing rarity-cap premise, then resubmit this field-tier rare-PN/PS frontier for review.
